description.narrative:
The objective of this support is Building Inclusive and Multi-dimensional Approaches and Capacities for Effective Conflict Prevention in Africa.
The intervention covers 3 result areas: 1) Enhanced Institutional Responses of the AU and RECS to Prevent Complex Conflicts 2) Strengthened Capacities of National and Local Infrastructures for Effective Conflict Prevention 3) Enhanced Evidence Based Analysis to Inform Policy Support and Knowledge Production for Conflict Prevention
Key constituencies to the programme include local, national, and regional structures, such as the AU, RECs/RMs (IGAD, SADC, ECCAS), and other organisations such as the United Cities and Local Governments; Youth focused and youth-led organisations, Women focused, and women led organisations and Networks (FemWise-Africa and GIMAC); Community leaders; and Faith-based and traditional leaders.

Nyckelaktörer för programmet inkluderar lokala, nationella och regionala strukturer, såsom AU, REC/RMs (IGAD, SADC, ECCAS) och andra organisationer som Förenta Städer och lokala myndigheter; ungdomsorganisationer, kvinnoorganisationer och nätverk (FemWise-Africa och GIMAC); lokala ledare; och trosbaserade- och traditionella ledare

title.narrative: African Centre for the Constructive Resolution of Dispute (ACCORD)

description.narrative:
Outcome 1 Institutional responses (AU, RECs, policy and structures)
- Establishment and operationalisation of the FemWise South Sudan Local Chapter as a national mechanism for womens participation in mediation. (p. 9) - Launch and institutionalisation of the Network of Women Mediators in Southern Africa within SADC structures. (p. 9) - Establishment and strengthening of the ECCAS Regional Women Mediators Network, including capacity to respond to election-related conflicts. (p. 9) - Contribution to the revision of the AU Mediation Handbook, improving policy relevance to current conflict dynamics. (p. 9) - Strengthened inter-regional coordination between COMESA and SADC mediation structures, supporting joint learning and collaboration. (p. 910) - Development and support to YPS policy frameworks and implementation roadmaps within IGAD and SADC. (p. 910)
Outcome 2 National and local capacities (behavioural and practical application)
Strengthened capacity of Local Peace Committees in Eswatini, improving their ability to respond to local conflict dynamics. (p. 10) Increased skills and confidence among REFWOMEN members, leading to improved readiness to coordinate local peace interventions. (p. 10) Contribution to South Africas second-generation WPS National Action Plan, strengthening policy continuity. (p. 10) Strengthened linkages between regional frameworks and national implementation of WPS and YPS commitments. (p. 10) Evidence of multiplier effects, with beneficiaries applying skills in mediation, dialogue facilitation, advocacy and policy processes in multiple countries (e.g. Sierra Leone, Namibia, Cameroon). (p. 10) Beneficiaries reporting use of mediation tools to prevent escalation of conflicts at community level. (p. 12)
Outcome 3 Knowledge and evidence-based analysis
Production and dissemination of key knowledge products (AJCR, Conflict Trends, Conflict and Resilience Monitor, Policy and Practice Briefs). (p. 11) Increased use of publications in research, policy development, training and advocacy by practitioners and academics. (p. 11) Recognition and indexing of AJCR, enhancing visibility and credibility of African scholarship. (p. 11) Evidence that knowledge products inform programming on issues such as sexual violence and local peacebuilding. (p. 11)
Cross-cutting results (effectiveness and behavioural change)
- 93% of participants reported learning new skills from programme activities. (p. 4) - 96% expressed confidence in applying acquired skills in their work. (p. 4)
93% reported sharing knowledge with others, demonstrating multiplier effects. (p. 4) Beneficiaries reported conducting dialogues, training peers, facilitating mediation and integrating gender perspectives in their work. (p. 12)
Sustainability-related results
- Continued functioning and development of women mediator networks (e.g. South Sudan, DRC) beyond programme support. (p. 1617)
- Evidence of institutional uptake, with organisations such as CSC and FECCLAHA integrating programme approaches into their core operations. (p. 16)
- Ongoing use and dissemination of knowledge products across networks and institutions. (p. 17)
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
